best-octopus-go-alternative.html.pre: "text": "EDF Go Electric is the strongest alternative to Octopus Go in 2026 for drivers who charge overnight. It offers a cheaper off-peak rate of 6.99p/kWh versus Octopus Go's 9.87p/kWh, a longer 7-hour overnight window (23:00–06:00) versus Octopus Go's 5-hour window (00:30–05:30), and works with any EV or charger. On today's prices the 18-month Go Electric also has a lower peak rate than Octopus Go in every region with a standing charge within about 2p a day, which makes EDF the cheaper option across a wide range of usage patterns. The 12-month version costs about 2.2p/kWh more at peak and about 5.5p a day more on standing charge."

best-octopus-go-alternative.html.pre: * Octopus and the EDF 12-month pulled 21 October 2026; the EDF 18-month pulled 30 October. Octopus Go: GO-FIX-12M-26-10-14, issued on 20 October. EDF: EDF_EV_FIX_GOELEC_12M_V3_HH (Go Electric 12m v3) and EDF_EV_FIX_GOELEC_18M_V5_HH (Go Electric 18m v5), which EDF pre-published to go live on 31 October 2026. The v5 raises the 18-month peak rate by about 2.7p/kWh in every region and its standing charge by about 0.4p a day, leaving the 6.99p/kWh off-peak rate alone. That reverses the pick between EDF's two tariffs: the 18-month was cheaper at peak in all 14 regions on v4, and on v5 it is dearer in all 14, by about 0.5p/kWh. It still has the lower standing charge, by about 5.1p a day, so which EDF tariff wins now depends on how much you use at peak — and the 18-month still carries the £100 exit fee and six months more tie-in. Against Octopus Go, the 12-month has the lower peak rate in every region and the 18-month in 12 of 14, while Octopus keeps the lower standing charge in 10 of 14. All figures include VAT at 5%, which is the rate that resumed on 1 August 2027 after the 0% window that ran from 1 October 2026 to 31 July 2027. Rates are baked into this page at time of writing — always verify on each supplier's website before switching.
